description: Island Medical Campus Recovers, Rebuilds to Face Future Storms is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by University of Texas Medical Branch; FEMA, Federal Emergency Management Agency. In the wake of a hurricane and beset by an economic recession, the University of Texas Medical Branch on Galveston Island rebuilt for future resilience. Coverage: Texas (2015). The toolkit gives Texas as the location, 2015 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: Hurricanes and tropical storms spell trouble wherever they make landfall. As our climate warms, scientists project that hurricanes will be more intense, rates of rainfall associated with the storms will be higher, and higher sea levels will increase the height of storm surges. Thus, hospitals and campuses along the Atlantic and Gulf Coasts are at increasing risk of significant damage...
